brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Decay Calculator" that helps elderly users with dementia track which of their memories are becoming harder to recall, visualized as a garden where each memory is repr

dominant_strengths: Poetic metaphor of a garden mapping memory vitality is conceptually appropriate and emotionally tender for the dementia context.
Soft cream-to-earth gradient evokes a horizon, lending a calm, contemplative atmosphere fitting elderly users.
Restrained palette and gentle stem heights communicate decay states (faded, thriving) without harsh medicalization.
dominant_weaknesses: Massive empty upper canvas wastes 70% of viewport while flowers crowd the bottom edge, breaking spatial balance.
Labels overlap petals and stems, making the three memory entries hard to read—critical failure for elderly low-vision users.
Only three flowers shown despite '12 memories planted' stat; the system feels underpopulated and inconsistent with its own data.
fix_priorities: Reflow flowers across the full ground band and enlarge typography to meet elderly accessibility minimums.
Resolve label collisions by anchoring captions below the soil line with clear hierarchy and contrast.
Show all 12 memories with visual decay encoding (opacity, wilt, size) so the metaphor matches the metric.
Add interaction affordances—tap to water/recall—to fulfill the 'calculator' and tracking promise behaviorally.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral metaphor and reflective poetry are present, but behavioral usability collapses under unreadable labels and a near-empty canvas.
rationale.intent_fit: The garden metaphor fits the brief beautifully in concept, but execution underdelivers on tracking, legibility, and dementia-appropriate clarity.
